skill.description: Use Neon PostgreSQL with serverless drivers, connection pooling, branching workflows, and deployment patterns for JavaScript and TypeScript applications.

skill.author: Asmayaseen

content.value_statement: Serverless Postgres setup can be slow when connection mode, pooling, and branching choices are unclear. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code practical Neon examples, templates, and workflow guidance.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to use Neon HTTP queries or WebSocket pooling.
Shows JavaScript and TypeScript setup for @neondatabase/serverless.
Provides a reusable database connection template for common app patterns.
Documents Neon branching commands and preview branch workflows.

use_cases.title: Set Up Serverless Queries
use_cases.description: Application developers can choose HTTP queries for edge routes, server actions, and simple CRUD flows.

use_cases.title: Plan Preview Branches
use_cases.description: Platform engineers can model pull request branches, migrations, and cleanup steps before implementing CI.

use_cases.title: Add Drizzle Integration
use_cases.description: Backend teams can compare Neon HTTP and WebSocket options for type-safe database access.

prompt_templates.title: Connect a New App
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the neon-postgres skill to explain the simplest Neon setup for a TypeScript app. Include the recommended connection method and required environment variable.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Connection Mode
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare Neon HTTP queries and WebSocket pooling for my Next.js app. Recommend one for API routes, server actions, and transactions.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Branch Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced CI and preview environment planning.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Neon branching workflow for pull request previews. Include branch creation, migration timing, environment variables, and cleanup.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Production Database Layer
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Neon database access plan for serverless limits, pooling choices, Drizzle usage, migration safety, and secret handling. Flag risky assumptions.

output_examples.input: Choose a Neon connection strategy for a Next.js app with server actions and occasional transactions.
output_examples.output: Recommended HTTP driver for server actions and simple reads. Use a WebSocket pool only for transaction-heavy paths.

output_examples.input: Plan CI preview databases for pull requests.
output_examples.output: Create a branch per pull request, run migrations against that branch, expose its URL as CI environment data, and delete it after merge.

output_examples.input: Review my Drizzle setup for Neon.
output_examples.output: Use the Neon HTTP adapter for serverless query paths. Keep direct migration credentials separate from pooled application credentials.

best_practices: Use environment variables for connection strings and keep real values out of source control.
Prefer parameterized queries or ORM builders for user-supplied values.
Use separate Neon branches for preview, staging, and production work.
anti_patterns: Hardcoding real database URLs in templates, prompts, or committed files.
Using a WebSocket pool for every serverless request without connection planning.
Running migrations against production from preview or feature environments.

faq.question: Does this skill run Neon CLI commands?
faq.answer: No. It documents commands and workflows so the user or agent can decide what to run.

faq.question: Does it need my database password?
faq.answer: It expects users to provide connection strings in environment variables. The skill does not include real credentials.

faq.question: Which apps fit this skill?
faq.answer: It fits JavaScript and TypeScript apps that use Neon, Next.js, Drizzle, edge functions, or serverless routes.

faq.question: Can it help with connection pooling?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains when to use HTTP queries, WebSocket pools, direct URLs, and pooled URLs.

faq.question: Can it create preview branches?
faq.answer: It provides branch workflow examples. It does not call the Neon API or create branches by itself.

faq.question: Is it a replacement for Neon docs?
faq.answer: No. It is a focused implementation guide and should be checked against current Neon product limits.
